items.title: The number of irreducible components of the generic fibre is a lower bound in a neighbourhood
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism over an irreducible base, if the generic fibre has n irreducible components then every fibre over a nonempty open has at least n irreducible components. The proof decomposes the generic fibre into its components, spreads the closures of those components to a neighbourhood using finite type and the irreducibility of the base, and then shows that the spread components remain distinct in each nearby fibre. Keeping the spread components distinct is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 7401-7429.
